metadata.name: SpeedKetchup
metadata.description: SpeedKetchup runs an internet speed test every 10 minutes against the nearest speedtest.net server, stores the results in a csv file and shows them in a builtin web page. The web page has speed and latency charts with distributions of the displayed results, daily, monthly, time of day and time of week averages, and a sortable table of every result. Every result can also go to Prometheus (the last test is served at /metrics), to InfluxDB over the line protocol, and to an MQTT broker with Home Assistant discovery. A single statically linked binary of a few hundred kilobytes, the image has nothing else in it.
metadata.tagline: Periodic internet speed tests with charts in a builtin web page
metadata.author: gatispei

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_SERVER
environment_variables.description: Speedtest server host[:port] to always test against. Empty picks the server with the lowest latency for every test.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_DOWNLOAD_DURATION
environment_variables.description: Seconds to test the download speed, 0 skips the download test.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_UPLOAD_DURATION
environment_variables.description: Seconds to test the upload speed, 0 skips the upload test.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_DOWNLOAD_CONNECTIONS
environment_variables.description: Parallel connections for the download test.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_UPLOAD_CONNECTIONS
environment_variables.description: Parallel connections for the upload test.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_INFLUX_URL
environment_variables.description: InfluxDB line protocol write url to also write every result to, http only, eg http://influxdb:8086/api/v2/write?org=home&bucket=speedketchup. Empty writes nowhere.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_INFLUX_TOKEN
environment_variables.description: Token for the InfluxDB write url.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_MQTT
environment_variables.description: MQTT broker host[:port] to also publish every result to, with Home Assistant discovery, plain mqtt only, port 1883 by default. Empty publishes nowhere.

environment_variables.name: SPEEDKETCHUP_MQTT_USER
environment_variables.description: User name for the MQTT broker.

volumes.description: Where the test results csv file is stored.

ports.description: Web page with the test results, Prometheus metrics at /metrics

before_install.en_us: The first test runs right after the start, the next ones every 10 minutes. Every test downloads and uploads for 10 seconds at full speed, so on a metered connection raise the interval or shorten the durations in the settings.
